request.spec:
A person may name other people on the sheet as their patrons, one at a time from their row (not
themselves, and not the same person twice; a refusal shows an error on the row; PATRON_ADDED
name=<name> patron=<patron name>). Show each person's patrons (names, comma and space separated,
sorted) and their backing: their patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a, 0.00 with no
patrons.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may name other people on the sheet as their patrons, one at a time from their row (not
themselves, and not the same person twice; a refusal shows an error on the row; PATRON_ADDED
name=<name> patron=<patron name>). Show each person's patrons (names, comma and space separated,
sorted) and their backing: their patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a, 0.00 with no
patrons.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Patrons and backing are in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests.

**What it does**
- Each person's row has a patron picker (`person-patron-select`), an add button (`person-patron-add`), and an error (`person-patron-error`) that shows when the server refuses. Choosing yourself, choosing someone who is already your patron, or choosing an unknown person is refused, and nothing is written.
- The row shows the patrons' names sorted and comma-separated (`person-patrons`), and their backing (`person-backing`): the patrons' due-totals added up, skipping n/a, and 0.00 when there are none. Backing is worked out on the front end with the same due-total function the "Due" column uses, so the two always agree, including when a patron is on hold.
- A successful add writes `PATRON_ADDED sheet=… by=… name=<name> patron=<patron name>` to the audit file.

**Stored data and server**
- A new table, `person_patron`, added by migration `V22__person_patron.sql`. It stores patron ids rather than names.
- A new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/patrons`, wired in YAML like the hold and retire endpoints.
- The person response now includes `patronIds`, loaded for each person.

**One change you didn't ask for:** on the first full run, scenario 3 failed at an unrelated step. On vic's freshly opened page, the test helper read a claim's status before the claim rows had appeared, so it reported that a refused "open" had succeeded. The server had in fact refused it: no `CLAIM_OPENED` line was written. The cause was that the active sheet id appeared on screen before that sheet's people and claims had loaded. I changed `SheetLoader.tsx` to fetch the people and claims first, and only then mark the sheet active. After that, all four tests passed. One side effect: if either fetch fails, the screen now shows the "could not be loaded" error instead of an empty sheet.

The new feature is in `src/main/frontend/features/patrons/patrons.slot.tsx`, plus the new classes under `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/person/`.
